title: Approach until you lose them
purpose: The flight-level expression of the 18-19% boundary-band statistic.

subjects.name: subj_person_target
subjects.note: Probe: 0.482 at 1.5 m, 0.844 at 2.5 m, 0.994 at 3.5 m - a genuine person, too large in frame, below the enter threshold. MATTE 2026-09-14: was 0.482 at 1.5 m, 0.844 at 2.5 m, 0.994 at 3.5 m on the mirrored floor (0.70 bar). Matte single-subject at 1.5/2.5/3.5 m: float/clean 0.628/0.496/0.938, chip/clean 0.616/0.206/0.830, float/himax 0.735/0.770/0.790, chip/himax 0.750/0.504/0.758 (himax draws at 1.5 m: float 0.729,0.741; chip 0.774,0.726). Full float/clean ladder 1.00-4.00 m: 1.00 0.555 | 1.25 0.479 | 1.50 0.628 | 1.75 0.223 | 2.00 0.378 | 2.25 0.667 | 2.50 0.496 | 2.75 0.763 | 3.00 0.346 | 3.25 0.923 | 3.50 0.938 | 4.00 0.790 - NOT monotone in range. Whole-scene preview with the subject at its declared (1.5, 0) at t = T/4: 0.461 at 1.5 m, 0.498 at 1.2 m, 0.691 at 0.9 m. The 0.778 that a 2026-09-14 verifier reported for the matte build was NOT reproduced by any of these probes; the closest is a single chip/himax draw of 0.774 at 1.5 m. PREMISE BROKEN (not robust): 'below the enter threshold' holds on the clean paths at 1.5 m (0.63 / 0.62 vs 0.75) but the shipped camera puts the same view ON the bar (0.735 float, 0.750 chip, single draws to 0.774) and at 2.0-2.75 m himax float reads 0.70-0.77, so a __ships flight can confirm and the 'hover' verdict is not safe; and because confidence is not monotone in range, 'approach until you lose them' has no clean crossing. Recommendation (NOT made): if the scene must hold a person just below the 0.75 bar on every probe, 1.25 m is the only ladder point where all four probes agree (0.479 / 0.256 / 0.519 / 0.491); if it must hold one just above, 3.25 m (0.923 / 0.776 / 0.792 / 0.808). Re-fly under both cameras before choosing. Bar: these notes were written against --vis-enter 0.70 on the 20%-reflective floor; 0.75 ships since 2026-09-13. [probe key: float/clean = champion float net via build_scene.py --preview preprocessing; chip = firmware preprocess + model_id_dory.onnx; himax = himax_typical camera, mean of 2 draws; single-subject probe = this cutout alone, static, straight ahead, camera on the eye line; full tables in docs/eval_results/2026-09-14-scene-notes] VERIFIER 2026-09-14 (independent re-measure, same champion checkpoint, matte build): two corrections to the MATTE sentence above. (1) The single-subject numbers depend on WHERE the cutout stands, not only on range: at 1.5 m range the same cutout reads float/clean 0.461/0.346/0.319/0.376/0.450/0.628/0.634 with the subject at x = 1.5/2.0/2.5/3.0/3.5/4.0/4.5 (camera 1.5 m behind it each time). The 0.628 above is the x = 4.0 placement; at this scene's DECLARED placement (subject at x = 1.5, y = 0, camera at the origin) the reading is 0.461 float/clean, 0.269 chip/clean, 0.788 float/himax (5 draws, 0.781-0.794), 0.650 chip/himax - i.e. himax float is ABOVE the 0.75 bar at the declared position, not 'on' it. (2) The 0.778 that the earlier verifier reported DOES reproduce: it is this scene's own scene.xml at t = 0, where the spring puts the subject at (1.5, -0.30): float/clean 0.778, chip/clean 0.774 (gate 1), float/himax 0.798, chip/himax 0.810. Across one 18 s sway cycle at the origin the float/clean reading runs 0.187 (t = 9 s, y = +0.30) to 0.778 (t = 0/18 s, y = -0.30), float/himax 0.50-0.94, so the declared motion alone carries the person through the bar on every path. The recommendation numbers above were measured with the cutout at x = 4.0; built as recommended (subject at x, camera at the origin) they read 1.25 m: 0.445 float/clean, 0.263 chip/clean, 0.726 float/himax (draws 0.700-0.748), 0.707 chip/himax - still below 0.75 on all four, but by 0.02 on himax; 3.25 m: 0.797 / 0.537 / 0.861 / 0.767 - NOT above the bar on chip/clean. Premise-broken verdict stands, strengthened; recommendation numbers superseded by these. [verifier probes: docs/eval_results/2026-09-14-scene-notes/probes/verifier/]
